bugs: app/Jobs/PushStockAllocations.php:45,74: synced_at is set to the time the job read the rows, and readiness checks updated_at > synced_at at second precision. v.rationale:
I rank impl-1 first. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 26 tests; impl-1: 22). Both use the modern attribute APIs (#[Signature], #[Scope], #[Fillable], the queue attributes), which I checked exist in Laravel 13.40. Both give up on retries before the 15-minute claim expires and clear the claim in failed(); a sync-queue probe confirmed that failed rows become ready again in both.

The deciding difference is how each records a sync. Impl-2 stores the time the job read the rows. With second-precision timestamps and a strict updated_at > synced_at check, an edit made in the same second just after that read is never synced. A probe showed this: impl-2 failed it and impl-1 passed. Impl-1 records the claim time (synced_at = sync_started_at), so an edit at worst causes one harmless resend. Impl-1 also writes the sync and disable updates in one transaction, uses tooManyRequests(), and its claim loop is simpler.

Impl-2 has the better test suite: more coverage and a Retry-After dataset. Its schedule is also more defensive, with withoutOverlapping as well as onOneServer. Those advantages don't outweigh the lost-update bug.
